title: DynamoDB resilience — PITR + Streams + stub stream Lambda

answers.explanation: PITR restore-table-to-point-in-time creates a new table within 35 days — never overwrites the source (Night 18 lab + Night 15 PITR trap).
KEYS_ONLY omits attribute values — no old/new viewCount in the stream record.
StartingPosition LATEST skips history before mapping creation — bump after mapping to test (night-18 setup -VerifyStream).
ADD is atomic increment; read-modify-write SET races under concurrent wiki traffic.
Streams deliver at-least-once — stub logging handler is idempotent; counters need conditional/idempotent design.
Night 18 DynamoDB Streams vs Night 17 SQS event source mapping — different decoupling sources.
Global tables for multi-Region DynamoDB active-active — awareness read in Night 18 block 3.
Gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB avoids NAT on DynamoDB API traffic (Night 8 Q10 pattern).
PAY_PER_REQUEST fits spiky wiki views — no RCU/WCU planning (Night 18 lab table).
AWS Backup centralizes policies across DynamoDB, RDS, EBS — Night 19 preview; PITR is per-table only.
Global tables: last writer wins; eventual cross-Region consistency — not strong global locks.
GSA split from Night 15–17 — Aurora JOIN reports vs DynamoDB hot counters.
Standard Lambda logging permissions — night-18-lab Ensure-Role policy pattern.
DynamoDB PITR max 35 days — Night 15 quiz Q10 trap (not 14 or 365).
Night 18 teardown is isolated study stack — Aurora and SQS unchanged (mirrors Night 17 Q12 logic).
